text: The exact same flow of data — from a source system through transformations to a final report — can be shown at two very different altitudes, and conflating them is a common mistake. This lesson covers business lineage versus technical lineage, and who each one is actually for.

Business lineage describes that journey in terms a non-technical stakeholder already understands — domain concepts, system names, plain-language steps. 'Customer Lifetime Value on the executive dashboard comes from the CRM and the billing system, combined in the data warehouse.' No tables, no column names, no code — just enough to answer where does this come from and can I trust it.

Technical lineage describes the same journey at the level engineers actually need to debug or change it — specific tables, specific columns, specific transformation logic, specific job names. 'dbo.CLV_Summary.LifetimeValueUSD is computed in sp_CalculateCLV by summing Billing.Invoices.AmountPaid joined to CRM.Accounts on AccountID, filtered to Status equals Active.' Precise enough to trace a bug, meaningless to most business stakeholders.

Picking only technical lineage leaves business stakeholders unable to answer basic trust questions themselves — every 'where does this number come from' question becomes a ticket to the data team. Picking only business lineage leaves engineers without enough detail to perform real impact analysis — 'the warehouse' isn't specific enough when one column breaks. Mature practices maintain both over the same underlying journey.

The two views answer different questions. Business lineage answers 'can I trust this number, and roughly where is it from' — what an executive or auditor actually asks. Technical lineage answers 'exactly what breaks if I change this column' — what an engineer writing SQL actually asks. Same journey, different altitude, different reader.

A quick test: if a diagram's boxes are named things like CRM, Billing System, and Executive Dashboard, you're looking at business lineage. If the boxes are named dbo.Accounts, stg.Invoices_Clean, and sp_CalculateCLV, you're looking at technical lineage. Neither is better — they're built for different readers, from the same underlying truth.
Next up: column-level versus table-level lineage — a second axis of granularity that applies within technical lineage itself, once you're already looking at the detailed, object-level view.
